title: Mega Millions Jackpot Soars to $743 Million After No Winner in Tuesday Drawing
excerpt: The prize, now the 10th largest in Mega Millions history, rolls to Friday as both major U.S. lotteries top $500 million simultaneously.
body:
• No ticket matched all six numbers in Tuesday's $707 million Mega Millions drawing; the jackpot now stands at an estimated $743 million, with a cash option of $323.4 million
  • The next drawing is Friday, July 24, at 11 p.m. ET, with odds of winning at roughly 1 in 302.6 million
  • Powerball's jackpot has also climbed to $567 million, putting combined lottery prizes above $1.3 billion this week
  • Non-U.S. citizens, including visa holders and green card holders, can legally buy tickets and claim prizes, though they face a higher 30% federal tax withholding

The Mega Millions jackpot surged to an estimated $743 million after no ticket matched all six winning numbers in Tuesday night's drawing, making it the 10th largest prize in the game's history and the biggest of 2023. The cash lump-sum option stands at $323.4 million.

The winning numbers drawn on July 21 were 25, 37, 59, 68, and 70, with a Mega Ball of 10, according to MegaMillions.com. While the top prize went unclaimed, two players walked away with multi-million-dollar consolation wins — a ticket sold in California won $2 million with a 2x Megaplier, and another in Arizona claimed $3 million with a 3x Megaplier.

"You do not need to be a resident or citizen to win."

— Mega Millions, Official FAQ

A Rare Double Surge

The Mega Millions surge comes alongside a Powerball jackpot that has climbed to $567 million for Wednesday night's drawing, marking a rare moment when both major U.S. lotteries exceed $500 million simultaneously. The Powerball prize has been growing since its last win on May 2, when winners in Florida and Texas split a $20 million jackpot, according to USA Today.

Combined, the two jackpots represent more than $1.3 billion in potential winnings this week, drawing heightened attention from ticket buyers across 45 states, the District of Columbia, and the U.S. Virgin Islands.

The Mega Millions jackpot has been rolling since March 17, when a player in Ohio won a comparatively modest $60 million on St. Patrick's Day. Before that, a $533 million prize was claimed by a single winner in Illinois on March 10, according to the Commercial Appeal.

What Winners Would Take Home

Mega Millions tickets cost $5 each and now include a built-in multiplier that can boost non-jackpot prizes by up to 10 times — a feature that previously required an additional dollar. Winners of Friday's jackpot can choose between the full $743 million annuity paid in 30 graduated installments, each 5% larger than the last, or the $323.4 million lump-sum cash option.

Federal taxes take a significant bite either way. U.S. citizens and resident aliens face a 24% federal withholding on prizes, according to California Lottery guidelines. State taxes vary widely — California, Florida, Texas, and several other states impose no state tax on lottery prizes, while New York withholds up to 10.9%.

What Indian Americans Should Know:

For members of the Indian diaspora on work visas, student visas, or other non-immigrant status, the rules are straightforward: anyone physically present in a participating state can purchase a ticket and claim a prize, regardless of citizenship. Both Mega Millions and Powerball confirm this on their official websites.

However, non-resident aliens face a steeper 30% federal tax withholding on lottery winnings, compared to 24% for citizens and permanent residents. There is no U.S.-India tax treaty provision that reduces this rate for gambling or lottery income. Winners must also file IRS forms and may need an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number to claim their prize.

What's Next

The next Mega Millions drawing is Friday, July 24, at 11 p.m. ET. If no one claims the prize, the jackpot could approach $800 million heading into the following Tuesday's draw. Wednesday night's Powerball drawing, with its $567 million prize, offers another shot at a nine-figure windfall.

The largest Mega Millions jackpot ever won remains the $1.602 billion prize claimed by a single ticket in Florida in August 2023. The current $743 million jackpot would need to roll several more times to challenge that record.
